 Joseph Arangio Mon, November 9, 2026 at 4:10 PM UTC 3 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Nicolas Cage Gained 25 Pounds for His New Movie, but Now He's Using One Machine to Lose It Nicolas Cage gained 25 pounds to portray NFL legend John Madden. Now the 62-year-old actor is working to shed the extra weight, and his chosen workout is surprisingly ordinary: the elliptical machine.
 In interviews published November 6 by People and Entertainment Weekly , Cage described the dietary changes behind his transformation and his return to cardio. With Madden approaching its November 18 release, his experience offers a look at the physical demands of playing one of football's most recognizable personalities.

 Related: Scientists Found a Surprising Link Between Sleeping 5 Hours and Feeling Hungrier 
 How Nicolas Cage Gained 25 Pounds to Play John Madden
 Cage didn't rely solely on prosthetics to resemble the former Oakland Raiders coach and NFL broadcaster. He deliberately increased his food intake, including pasta and sourdough bread, to add weight for the role.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The transformation helped prepare him to portray Madden, whose larger-than-life presence made him a familiar figure to generations of football fans.
 But gaining weight for a movie and maintaining a healthy body composition are different objectives. Actors can make temporary physical changes for a production that wouldn't necessarily be appropriate as long-term fitness strategies.
 Related: Your Walking Speed May Reveal a Surprising Clue About How Well You're Aging 
 Related: Russell Crowe Lost 55 Pounds After Making One Surprisingly Simple Lifestyle Change 
 Why Cage Is Using the Elliptical to Lose Weight
 Rather than describing an extreme training regimen, Cage identified elliptical workouts as part of his effort to reverse the weight gain.
 Advertisement Advertisement The machine provides aerobic exercise without the repetitive impact associated with running. That can make it an accessible option for adults who want cardiovascular conditioning while managing joint stress.
 However, elliptical exercise alone doesn't guarantee weight loss. Overall energy intake, workout consistency, sleep, and individual health factors also influence results.
 Related: Dwayne Johnson Lost 50 Pounds but Refused to Use an Extreme Weight-Loss Diet 
 What Cage's Transformation Means for Fitness After 60
 Cage's experience illustrates a distinction between preparing for a role and building sustainable fitness.
 For adults over 60, aerobic exercise can support cardiovascular health, while resistance training helps preserve strength and muscle mass during weight loss. Combining both is generally more useful than focusing exclusively on the scale.
 Advertisement Advertisement Cage hasn't established a public timeline for losing all 25 pounds, so his elliptical routine shouldn't be interpreted as a guaranteed formula.
 The takeaway: A Hollywood transformation may attract attention, but sustainable progress still comes down to consistent exercise, sensible nutrition, and realistic expectations.
